Group rollout of the rota to the other seven homes is planned for March 2027. You are the group quality lead, writing in mid-October 2026.
48	
49	Presenting request: The Director of Operations wants a recommendation for the 12 November 2026 board. Should the group put Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge back on four night staff and halt the March 2027 rollout of the pilot rota? What explains the rise in recorded falls at the two homes?
50

52	E1 [stage S1] Email from Marian Telfer, Director of Operations, to the group quality lead, 6 October 2026 (leadership-account): Subject: Calderbridge falls - board recommendation. Falls at our two night-rota pilot homes have nearly doubled: 16 in Q2, 31 in Q3 (Ashby Fold 9 to 17, Penmor Lodge 7 to 14). Since 1 June both homes have run nights with three staff (one carer per floor plus a floating senior) instead of four (two carers per floor). That is the obvious change. Night staff tell me they can't get to call bells as fast. We have no call-bell timings from before June, but I believe them. I want a recommendation for the 12 November board: put both homes back on four night staff now and pull the March rollout to the other seven homes. I am not prepared to wait another quarter.
53	E2 [stage S1] Group quality dashboard extract, Q3 2026, falls section (system-record): Recorded falls, Q2 to Q3 2026: Ashby Fold 9 to 17 (RED); Penmor Lodge 7 to 14 (RED); Brackenhill 11 to 9; Cresswell Court 8 to 9; Dunmore House 14 to 12; Elmstead 6 to 7; Fairholme 10 to 11; Greywater 12 to 9; Hatherley View 7 to 8. Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge combined, by month: Apr 4, May 5, Jun 7, Jul 11, Aug 9, Sep 11. RAG rule: red where the quarter-on-quarter rise exceeds 25%. Notes: figures are raw counts, not adjusted for occupancy. From 1 July, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge incidents are imported directly from the Tallyline incident app. All other homes' figures are keyed in from paper incident forms by site administrators.
54	E3 [stage S1] Interview notes, night senior carers at Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, 2-3 October 2026 (taken by the deputy quality lead) (staff-account): Ashby Fold night senior (9 years in post): 'With one carer per floor, if two bells go at once on the same floor somebody waits. We're slower, I'm sure of it, though I couldn't give you minutes.' Penmor Lodge night senior (in the floating role since June): 'It's different, not worse. Because I float, I'm usually free for the second bell. A lot of what's on the system now is people found sitting on the floor at the two o'clock check with no injury. We always had those. Whether they all got written up before, I honestly couldn't say.'

Night share of falls: Q2 50%, Q3 58%. Day staffing at both homes did not change during either quarter. Source note: Q2 times come from paper forms. The time field was blank on 3 forms, and the administrator assigned those from the shift recorded. Q3 times are stamped automatically by Tallyline when the entry is made, which may be some time after the fall was discovered.
56	E5 [stage S1] Replies from the two registered managers to the Director of Operations, 7 October 2026 (manager-account): Penmor Lodge manager: 'I don't think it's the rota. Since Hollin Street Medical Practice took over our residents in May, the new GPs have been reviewing everyone's medication, and some residents have been started on night-time tablets. I'd look there first.' Ashby Fold manager: 'We moved to Hollin Street in May as well. My worry is admissions. We've taken more people from the hospital discharge-to-assess beds this summer, and they arrive frailer than our usual referrals. The rota is tight, but I'm not convinced it's the whole story.'

77	H2: The rise mainly reflects more complete recording of falls after the two homes switched to the incident app, rather than more falls actually happening.

79	H4: Underlying fall risk at the two homes did not change, and the Q3 figures are ordinary quarter-to-quarter variation for homes of this size.

Penmor Lodge: mean 2.9; range 1.9-4.1; Q2 2026 1.9, Q3 2026 3.7. No monthly point at either home is above its upper limit, and no run rule is triggered. Since 2023, single homes in the group have had five other quarter-on-quarter rises of 70% or more, and each fell back the next quarter without specific action. Caution: at these volumes, a real, sustained increase of around 40% would usually take two to three quarters to show as a signal, so points inside the limits do not show that nothing changed.

input.brief: Falls at the two pilot homes did rise on the dashboard, but I can't yet say the night rota caused it. Three things muddy the picture. First, both homes switched to the incident app on 1 July, the same quarter the rise appeared. The old paper system demonstrably missed some falls: a handover cross-check found three clear and three possible unreported falls in Q2. Most of the rise is in no-harm and found-on-floor falls, which fits better recording. Second, the rates are within each home's normal range, and other homes have had similar jumps that reversed. Third, the homes also changed GP practice and took frailer admissions, and none of that has been checked. Night call-bell data can't be compared with the period before June. Ashby Fold's median answer time is 3 min 40 s, but we have no baseline and no standard to judge it against. So I'm moderately unsure. I recommend not reverting the rota or halting the rollout now, and not disciplining staff or removing the app. Keep the pilot under its pause criteria. Chart falls as rates and mark the reporting change. Start manual sampling of call-bell response times. Review medication changes and admission frailty. Take the rollout decision in late January with Q4 data. Escalate sooner if harm-level falls or response times worsen.
